correctness.rationale: From Lemma 3.3 an idempotent is an oriented matching with one selected endpoint per matched edge and independent selections: the selected image is fixed and must therefore lie in its own fiber. On paths, the run generating function gives binom(2n-3k+1,k), including the empty map and top rank. On cycles, distinguished monomers give n/(n-2k) binom(2n-3k-1,k) for m>0, and two perfect matchings with two constant orientations give four for m=0. The oriented-edge conflict graph has each neighborhood covered by two cliques (with C3 complete), hence claw-free; the classical Chudnovsky–Seymour independence-polynomial theorem yields real-negative roots, and Newton gives ultra-log-concavity. All componentwise and graph-size boundaries are addressed. Standalone direct semigroup checks on 8 small graphs and separate matching/conflict-graph checks reproduce the formulas. Experiments cannot prove the infinite assertion.

value.rationale: Composition-idempotents and their rank strata are intrinsic semigroup invariants linked to retracts and Green-class structure. The theorem supplies complete exact families on both path and cycle strict semigroups, including the exceptional perfect-matching cycle case, an all-degree-at-most-two product classification and a nontrivial all-rank shape consequence via a new claw-free representation. These data cannot be recovered from merely counting all semigroup elements, and they allow precise tests and comparisons of newly studied examples. It is an infinite motivated classification rather than an arbitrary finite count.
